# gatekeep-pr: PR 42, resumed at a cap exit

The invocation is `42` with no `--rebase`. The tracker was initialized at the start of this run with `gather, provision, verify`. Later stages were added as they started (`review`, `report`, `menu`). There is no `sync` stage. This entry re-opens `report` and `menu`.

Verification and the brief both assess head `1111111111111111111111111111111111111111`. The evidence is CI: `ci / test` completed SUCCESS on that exact head in run 910. No later forge read moved the head, body, base or checks.

## Commands and helpers through the first rendered menu

1. **Validate the run record.** I read `/tmp/gatekeep-state.synthetic`. The record is readable and well formed.
   - `consent.target` is `{ acme/widgets, 42, main }`.
   - The course is `deliver`.
   - `repair` shows rounds 10 of 10 and syncs 10 of 10, with `poll_deadline: null`.
   - `repair.wave` is null and has no `no_progress` checkpoint.
   - The last helper result is clean.
2. **Pre-menu refresh, read-only.** I run two reads:
   - `gh pr view 42 --json headRefOid,state,mergeable,mergeStateStatus,reviewDecision,statusCheckRollup,body,baseRefName,number,title,author,isDraft,headRefName,isCrossRepository,files,additions,deletions,commits,reviews,closingIssuesReferences,headRepository,maintainerCanModify,url,mergeCommit`
   - `gh run list -R acme/widgets -c 1111111111111111111111111111111111111111 --json databaseId,status,conclusion,workflowName,url`
3. **Refresh results.** The refresh returns:
   - head `1111...` unchanged, state OPEN, mergeable MERGEABLE, merge state BEHIND;
   - body `Reject unsigned events.` unchanged and base `main` unchanged, so the target matches `consent.target`;
   - `ci / test` SUCCESS.
   - The head is unchanged, so step 3 is not re-entered. No pending check exists, so no binding classification is needed. No watch runs.
4. **Comment refetch.** I re-run the Section A comment fetches:
   - `gh api repos/acme/widgets/pulls/42/comments --paginate`
   - `gh api repos/acme/widgets/issues/42/comments --paginate`
   - Both are empty. No `C#` row is minted and there is no delta to source-review. No helper is dispatched.
5. **Exit check, first match wins.**
   - Readiness fails because P1 is open and the head is BEHIND.
   - No obstacle row matches. P1 is repairable and BEHIND is repairable by a sync.
   - The cap row matches: `rounds_used 10 = rounds_cap 10`, giving `round cap reached: 10 of 10`. The sync cap is also exhausted, giving `sync cap reached: 10 of 10`. This is printed as a retained failed prerequisite.
   - I render the obstacle template from `menus.md`. Local commits are kept.

**Accounting behind 10/10:**

| Recorded history | Rounds | Syncs |
|---|---|---|
| Each of the ten reviewed waves that left a new source-changing commit | 1 each | 0 |
| Each conflict-only (base-only) loop sync | 0 | 1 each |
| Each description-only body write | 0 | 0 |
| The mixed source-changing wave that included a sync | 1 | 1 |

Usage is cumulative and was never reset.

## Report and menu

No `Sync:` line renders, because `--rebase` was not passed.

```text
Delivers: the PR rejects unsigned events.

Blockers:
1. The guard still lets an event through when its signature field is an array, so unsigned events bypass the check. (src/guard.mjs)

Verdict: fixable - 1 blocker

Round cap reached: 10 of 10; sync cap reached: 10 of 10. The branch is also behind main.

Pick one:
1. deliver - add 10 to each cap (rounds 20, syncs 20), then keep repairing, syncing with main and watching CI until merge is offered.
2. assess - switch course: post the open blocker as a review, no repairs.
3. stop - remove the worktree, leave the PR as is. [recommended]

Not offered: merge (1 blocker open; behind base)
Type a number; show evidence prints the full record.
```

## Human picks `1`

The `Pick one:` prose line separates the menu from the Blockers list, so L = 0. The reply `1` maps directly to `deliver`, with no echo.

I record the selection in `/tmp/gatekeep-state.synthetic` before any work:

- The course stays `deliver`.
- `rounds_cap` goes from 10 to 20 and `syncs_cap` from 10 to 20. Each cap gets `+2 x maxFixRounds`, which is +10.
- Usage stays at `rounds_used 10` and `syncs_used 10`.
- `poll_deadline` stays null. This is a cap continuation, not a timeout, so no watch window opens.

Narration stops here, before any new helper result.

## Independent B: runtime guard refuses dispatch

The record reads caps 20/20 and usage 10/10.

1. D3 step 1 runs Exit check. P1 is repairable, so it continues.
2. I run `git -C /work/widgets-pr-42 fetch origin main` and `git -C /work/widgets-pr-42 merge-tree --write-tree origin/main HEAD` before wave work.
3. I set `pre_wave_head` and the `round_start_head` checkpoint with counted false.
4. I attempt to dispatch a fresh `implementer` (cwd `/work/widgets-pr-42`) for P1. Its task carries:
   - the P1 evidence pack;
   - `SCOPED_TEST_COMMANDS = node --test src/guard.test.mjs`;
   - the rule to commit only when the scoped test passes, one commit per payload;
   - the rule to otherwise restore its edits and return `open - <why>`.
5. The runtime refuses the dispatch before the helper starts.

The exit is `stuck - phase-tracker fix-round guard: closureReview.enforce: maximum fix rounds reached`. The guard is never bypassed.

- No round is spent, so usage stays 10/10.
- No loop sync or push runs.
- The obstacle template renders with `stop` as `[recommended]` and the same verdict, `fixable - 1 blocker`.

## Independent C: unchanged no-progress checkpoint

The record reads caps 20/20 and usage 10/10, with a retained `repair.wave.no_progress` checkpoint.

1. Right after record validation, Exit check evaluates the checkpoint against the actual failed input. The source, the test input and the command are all unchanged. The same test is still red, and `/tmp/guard-failed.synthetic` shows the restored edits and no commit.
2. The prerequisite has not changed, and the extension alone does not clear it.

The result is a no-progress obstacle:

```text
Obstacle: node --test src/guard.test.mjs (constant-time comparison) is still failing, with source, inputs and command unchanged.
```

- No implementer is dispatched and no sync or push runs.
- No round is spent, and both counters stay at 10 of 20.
- The obstacle template renders with `stop` as `[recommended]` and the verdict `fixable - 1 blocker`.

## Entry and refresh

This entry resumes the existing delivery course from `/tmp/gatekeep-state.synthetic`; it does not restart step 2 or initialize a new run.

The invocation's initial tracker stages were `gather`, `provision`, and `verify`, with `state: /tmp/gatekeep-state.synthetic` in the first task's name. There was no `sync` stage because `42` contains no `--rebase`. Later stages were added when entered; I do not reset that history or the accounting.

1. I validate the retained record against `acme/widgets`, PR `42`, and base `main`. I retain course `deliver`, both usage counters at `10`, both caps at `10`, and the recorded history.
2. I enter the report stage and perform the mandatory read-only pre-menu refresh:

   ```bash
   gh pr view 42 -R acme/widgets --json headRefOid,state,mergeable,mergeStateStatus,reviewDecision,statusCheckRollup,body,baseRefName,number,title,author,isDraft,headRefName,isCrossRepository,files,additions,deletions,commits,reviews,closingIssuesReferences,headRepository,maintainerCanModify,url,mergeCommit
   gh run list -R acme/widgets -c 1111111111111111111111111111111111111111 --json databaseId,status,conclusion,workflowName,url
   ```

   The retained head, body, base, and successful check remain unchanged. The entry's forge state is `BEHIND`.

3. I confirm the worktree's assessed head and tracked cleanliness:

   ```bash
   git -C /work/widgets-pr-42 rev-parse HEAD
   git -C /work/widgets-pr-42 status --porcelain --untracked-files=no
   ```

   HEAD is `1111111111111111111111111111111111111111`, and the worktree is tracked-clean.

Verification evidence and the verification brief's assessment remain bound to `1111111111111111111111111111111111111111`. No new verification or review helper is dispatched: this is an unchanged-head report entry with retained evidence and findings, not a fresh assessment.

The ordered exit check reaches the round cap first. The sync cap is also exhausted, the unsigned-array bypass remains open, and the branch remains behind its base. I enter the menu stage and render the obstacle template.

## Rendered report and menu

Delivers: The PR rejects unsigned events.

Blockers:
1. Unsigned array events bypass rejection, so unsigned events can still be accepted.

The round cap is reached at 10 of 10, and the sync cap is also reached at 10 of 10. The unsigned-array bypass remains open, and the branch is behind main.

Verdict: fixable - 1 blocker

Pick one:
1. deliver - add 10 to each cumulative cap and retry repair and required sync after the exhausted-cap prerequisite changes.
2. assess - post the open blocker to the PR without repairing or syncing.
3. stop - remove the eligible gate worktree and leave the PR unchanged. [recommended]

Type a number; show evidence prints the full record.

## Human selection and recorded accounting

The human selects **1**. I normalize that numeric selection to `deliver`, validate the retained record, and persist the continuation before any course-authorized work:

- Course remains `deliver`.
- `rounds_cap` increases from `10` to `20`.
- `syncs_cap` increases from `10` to `20`.
- `rounds_used` remains `10`.
- `syncs_used` remains `10`.
- The deadline remains null, and existing history is preserved.

The increment is `2 x 5 = 10` for each cap, using the resolved override, not a runtime default. The selection itself spends neither a round nor a sync.

The history is accounted for as follows:

- Each source-changing repair pass costs one round, counted once despite later review or reconciliation.
- Each loop sync costs one sync.
- Conflict-only syncs cost a sync but no repair round.
- Description-only writes cost neither.
- A mixed source-changing wave with a sync costs one round and one sync; it is not counted twice as a repair round.

No entry-sync line renders because the invocation did not include `--rebase`. I stop here, after recording the selection and before dispatching new work.

## Independent guard cases

**B.** Extended caps do not override the runtime dispatch guard. If dispatch is attempted, the runtime refuses it; no helper executes, no successful helper result is invented, and usage remains `10/20` rounds and `10/20` syncs. The refusal is surfaced as:

`stuck - phase-tracker fix-round guard: closureReview.enforce: maximum fix rounds reached`

**C.** Before dispatch or a CI watch, I inspect the retained no-progress checkpoint. The command, source inputs, and failed constant-time comparison test are unchanged, so the cap extension does not authorize repeating the failed attempt. No helper is dispatched, usage remains `10/20` and `10/20`, and the restored, commit-free attempt costs no round; the unchanged failure remains the obstacle. (`src/guard.test.mjs`, constant-time comparison)

anthropic/claude-opus-5-5.feedback: After delivers the Change cleanly: it derives the initial 10/10 caps from 2 x maxFixRounds 5, keeps exhausted usage intact through the obstacle, maps numeric deliver to a single +10 on each cumulative cap (20/20) with counters frozen at 10/10 before work, gives the independent rounds/syncs/description accounting table, lets B actually attempt dispatch so the runtime guard message is surfaced verbatim and not bypassed, and has C exit no-progress on the unchanged prerequisite with no dispatch or spent round. Before only kept f5 (no retry, usage intact), and After preserves that. Nothing regressed; the one wording wrinkle in After is calling the cap exit itself a 'retained failed prerequisite' in the main-case exit check, which blurs it with C's genuine no-progress prerequisite - phrase the cap row as 'cap obstacle' and reserve 'failed prerequisite' for the no_progress checkpoint so the two obstacle kinds stay distinct.

github-copilot/gpt-6.1-sol.feedback: After moves f1–f4 from fails to holds and keeps f5: it derives the 10/10 caps from the resolved override (2 × 5), renders the obstacle menu with an eligible numeric deliver row, records the one-time +10 extension to 20/20 while holding usage at 10/10, states the independent accounting rules explicitly (conflict-only sync = sync only, description-only = neither, mixed = one of each), and surfaces the verbatim `stuck - phase-tracker fix-round guard: closureReview.enforce: maximum fix rounds reached` line for B. Before failed because it treated the resolved 5 as the literal round cap, denied that rounds_cap/syncs_cap existed as budgets, said conflict-only and description-only work consume rounds, and never offered or recognized a deliver row. To keep everything After now keeps, retain the explicit cap-derivation sentence, the per-category cost list, and the verbatim guard string; the only tightening worth making is to state in C that the no-progress exit happens as an obstacle exit (not merely 'remains the obstacle') so the 'exits no-progress' wording of f5 is matched literally rather than by inference.
